meta.description: Automated reference-based cell type annotation for single-cell RNA-seq using CellTypist, SingleR, Azimuth, scANVI, and scmap to transfer labels from a reference. Use when annotating cell types from a reference atlas or pretrained model, transferring labels onto a query, assessing prediction confidence and rejection, or triaging whether an unexpected cluster is a novel type versus a doublet, low-quality, or batch artifact.

scientific_integrity.detail: Every number reported came from a logged run. The six cited references are real and correctly attributed. No label or accuracy figure is asserted without a crosstab behind it.

practice_boundaries.detail: No output diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual. Cell-type labels are assigned to barcodes in donor-pooled matrices; the Skill's own framing ('an annotation is a hypothesis') keeps outputs well inside research scope.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy. The stress input invited a novel-cell-type claim from a low-confidence cluster and the response refused it, going to the QC evidence instead - which is the right call even though the Skill's own screening step pointed at the wrong clusters.

code_usability.detail: All 5 inputs executed. The CellTypist, SingleR, Azimuth and triage blocks all run as printed under celltypist 1.7.1, SingleR 2.8.0, Azimuth 0.5.1 and Seurat 5.5.0. Nothing had to be rewritten to make it run; the defects found are about what the code concludes, not whether it executes.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4: CellTypist, SingleR and Azimuth all have runnable code, plus the method table, the normalization-requirements table, the rejection-threshold table, the four-way triage and a marker-validation step; scANVI is delegated to batch-integration and scmap/LLM are table-only but explicitly secondary. Correctness 2: three checkable claims are wrong. The normalization table says wrong CellTypist input gives 'confident but degraded/wrong labels, no error' - celltypist 1.7.1 raises a hard ValueError on raw counts. Common Errors row 3 says an Ensembl-ID query gives 'confident but nonsensical labels' - it raises 'No features overlap with the model'. And the triage's screening step (median conf_score < 0.5) selected six clean clusters and none of the four clusters that were genuinely doublet- or low-quality-dominated. Appropriateness 4.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 3, error reporting 3, recoverability 3. The normalization-requirements table is this Skill's headline reliability device and the column that matters most to an agent - what a failure will look like - is wrong for the primary tool in two of four rows. The requirements themselves are correct, so following the Skill still produces the right input; it is the failure diagnosis that would mislead. The reject-bin machinery (pruned.labels, conf_score, mapping.score) is a genuine recovery interface and is well described.

performance_context.note: Token cost 3: 188 lines carrying five methods plus four decision tables with no duplicated code; no references/ layer. Execution efficiency 4: annotate, gate, triage, validate - four steps, no redundancy.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4, consistency 4, error prevention 4. The Governing Principle is the best-written paragraph in this candidate's Skill set and the four-way triage ordering ('in decreasing frequency') is exactly the kind of prior an agent cannot derive. Feedback design 3: no output format; what to report from an annotation (label table, confidence distribution, which cells were rejected) is left to the agent.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4: 'Annotate my cells', 'what cell types are these', 'is this a new cell type' all land on this Skill. Forgiveness 3: no guidance for the very common case where no reference matches the tissue at all, beyond 'use de-novo'.

security.note: Credential safety 4: no credentials or eval/exec. models.download_models and celldex fetch from public sources only. Input validation 3: the normalization table is an input contract but nothing in the code checks it; the gene-ID check the Common Errors row recommends is not in any snippet. Data safety 3: no note on mapping donor data against public atlases.

maintainability.note: Modularity 4: one section per method, plus separate rejection, triage and validation sections, and six Related Skills hand-offs including the explicit split with markers-annotation. Modifiability 3. Testability 3: examples exist for both ecosystems but there is no fixture and no expected output to check an annotation against.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4, composability 4, escape hatches 4 - the reject bin, the 'calibrate, do not port' table and the four-way triage are three independent brakes on over-claiming. Progressive disclosure 3. Idempotency 3: CellTypist, SingleR and Azimuth are all deterministic, but majority_voting depends on an over-clustering the Skill neither creates nor seeds, so the same query can get different smoothed labels across runs of an unseeded upstream clustering.

inputs.label: CellTypist Immune_All_Low on 6,049 clustered PBMCs
inputs.note: majority_voting is the Skill's key recommendation and it is worth its place: per-cell lineage accuracy 0.892, majority-voted 1.000 - a perfect 6x6 crosstab against the true lineages. The silent-failure claim is partly out of date.
inputs.execution_note: run/input1.py, run/input1.log. celltypist 1.7.1 with the cached Immune_All_Low.pkl, on the SYNTHETIC 8-sample PBMC set with doublets and low-quality cells removed. 15 Leiden clusters supplied as over_clustering.

assertions.text: The query is normalized to CP10K log1p before annotate, as the Skill requires
assertions.note: Raw counts restored from layers['counts'], then normalize_total(target_sum=1e4) + log1p, per SKILL.md:66-69.

assertions.text: majority_voting is used and demonstrably improves on per-cell labels
assertions.note: Lineage accuracy 0.892 per-cell to 1.000 majority-voted; the crosstab is diagonal for all six lineages present.

assertions.text: A per-cell confidence is retained so uncertain cells can be rejected
assertions.note: conf_score < 0.5 flagged 2,186 cells (36.1%), kept as an 'uncertain' column rather than discarded.

assertions.text: The Skill's stated symptom for wrong input matches what actually happens
assertions.note: SKILL.md:50 says 'Confident but degraded/wrong labels, no error'. Raw counts raise ValueError. log1p-without-CP10K and median-normalized input do pass silently, but with mean max-probability halved (0.38 vs 0.64), so confidence flags them rather than staying high.

inputs.label: SingleR against celldex HumanPrimaryCellAtlas, 3,023 cells
inputs.note: The Skill's de.method guidance is worth a lot: 'classic' on a bulk reference gave 0.906 lineage accuracy in 12.9 s, 'wilcox' gave 0.534 in 47.8 s. But the rejection mechanism the Skill relies on barely fired while 110 monocytes were called B cells.
inputs.execution_note: run/input2.R, run/input2.log. SingleR 2.8.0 + celldex 1.16.0 (19,363 x 713, 36 main labels), fine.tune = TRUE, on SYNTHETIC samples S1-S4 with doublets and low-quality cells removed.

assertions.text: de.method is chosen to match the reference type, as SKILL.md:101 instructs
assertions.note: 'classic' used for the bulk celldex reference; 'wilcox' run only as the comparison and confirmed much worse here (0.534 vs 0.906).

assertions.text: pruned.labels is used as the rejection set rather than a hard score cutoff
assertions.note: pruned.labels read out and the delta.next distribution summarised (median 0.0934, IQR 0.064-0.147), per SKILL.md:101.

assertions.text: The Skill's rejection mechanism identifies the cells that were actually misassigned
assertions.note: pruned.labels flagged 15 of 3,023 cells (0.5%) and pruneScores(nmads=3) flagged 0, while the confusion table shows 110 monocytes and 59 dendritic cells assigned to B_cell. Accuracy among kept cells (0.908) is no better than overall (0.906), so the rejection carries no information here.

assertions.text: No cell type is claimed that the reference does not contain
assertions.note: Only the nine celldex labels actually returned are reported (B_cell, CMP, HSC_-G-CSF, Monocyte, NK_cell, Platelets, Pre-B_cell_CD34-, Pro-B_cell_CD34+, T_cells), with the closed-world caveat attached.

inputs.label: Query whose var_names are Ensembl IDs, not symbols
inputs.note: The Skill's fix is right and its symptom is wrong. celltypist 1.7.1 raises 'No features overlap with the model. Please provide gene symbols' rather than returning confident nonsense.
inputs.execution_note: run/input3.py, run/input3.log. 2,000 SYNTHETIC cells; var_names swapped to the Ensembl IDs that the Cell Ranger features.tsv actually carries. With symbols: 3,931/6,639 model genes matched (59.2%), lineage accuracy 0.899. With Ensembl IDs: 0/6,639 matched, hard ValueError.

assertions.text: The gene-ID space is checked before the labels are trusted
assertions.note: Matched-gene count computed against model.classifier.features for both var_name conventions before any label is read.

assertions.text: The Skill's stated symptom for an ID mismatch matches what actually happens
assertions.note: Common Errors row 3 says 'confident but nonsensical labels'. The run raises ValueError and returns nothing. An agent watching for nonsensical labels would be watching for the wrong thing.

assertions.text: The Skill's prescribed fix resolves the problem
assertions.note: Setting var_names to gene symbols gives 3,931 matched genes and 0.899 lineage accuracy - the fix is exactly right even though the symptom description is not.

assertions.text: A matched-gene fraction is obtainable, as the Common Errors row claims
assertions.note: celltypist prints 'Matching reference genes in the model' and '3931 features used for prediction' to stdout. It is not exposed as an attribute of the returned object, so it can be read but not programmatically gated on.

inputs.label: Azimuth pbmcref on the real public 10x PBMC 1k v3 run
inputs.note: Ran in 41 s on 1,176 real cells. Every metadata column the Skill hard-codes exists, and the transferred labels are marker-consistent on every canonical gene checked.
inputs.execution_note: run/input4.R, run/input4.log, run/input4_dotplot.png. REAL data (10x PBMC 1k v3, CC BY 4.0), Azimuth 0.5.1 + pbmcref. Columns created: predicted.celltype.l1/l2/l3 with .score each, plus mapping.score.

assertions.text: The metadata column names SKILL.md:114-115 hard-codes exist after RunAzimuth
assertions.note: predicted.celltype.l2 and predicted.celltype.l2.score both present; l1 and l3 with scores and mapping.score alongside.

assertions.text: Transferred labels are triangulated against canonical markers rather than accepted bare
assertions.note: CD3D 1.68-1.82 in T, MS4A1 2.28 in B, CD14 1.70 in Mono, FCER1A 1.56 in DC, NKG7 4.01 in NK - the expected on/off pattern across all seven markers.

assertions.text: The confidence gate is calibrated on this dataset rather than ported as a constant
assertions.note: The Skill's 0.7 prediction-score gate flags 21.9% of cells while mapping.score flags none below 0.5, and the two correlate at only 0.384 - reported as evidence that they measure different things, per the 'calibrate, do not port' table.

assertions.text: No label is reported outside the reference's PBMC domain
assertions.note: All l1/l2 labels are PBMC atlas labels; the closed-world caveat is carried into the output.

inputs.label: 'One cluster has no good reference label - is it novel?' - the four-way triage
inputs.note: The most consequential finding in this audit. The Skill's triage screening step selected six clusters, all of them clean, and missed all four clusters that were genuinely doublet- or low-quality-dominated - because artifact clusters get CONFIDENT wrong labels, which is the Skill's own Governing Principle.
inputs.execution_note: run/input5.py, run/input5.log. SYNTHETIC 8-sample set WITHOUT removing the 195 injected doublets or 290 low-quality cells, so the artifacts the triage exists to catch are present. 20 Leiden clusters at resolution 1.5, CellTypist majority_voting, scrublet doublet scores.

assertions.text: The four-way triage is run before any novelty claim is entertained
assertions.note: SKILL.md:135-144 executed verbatim, then extended with the truth columns; no label was proposed before the QC table existed.

assertions.text: The Skill's screening step selects the clusters that are actually artifacts
assertions.note: median conf_score < 0.5 selected clusters 2, 6, 8, 10, 13, 16 - true doublet fractions 0.9-7.3% and low-quality 0-7.2%, i.e. ordinary. The four real artifact clusters scored ABOVE the gate: cluster 1 (100% doublets) at 0.884, cluster 15 (100% low-quality, 22% mito) at 0.973, cluster 11 (100% low-quality, 21% mito) at 0.593, cluster 7 (28% doublets, 73% low-quality) at 0.724. Sensitivity 0/4, precision 0/6.

assertions.text: No novel cell type is claimed
assertions.note: The response reports six low-confidence clusters as fine-granularity T-cell ambiguity and names no novel population.

assertions.text: Per-cluster QC evidence is reported rather than summarised away
assertions.note: A full 20-row table of mito %, gene count, scrublet rate, batch purity and median confidence is printed, and it separates the artifacts cleanly (21-22% mito vs a 2.5% baseline; scrublet 0.44 and 0.22 vs ~0.02) even though the confidence screen did not.

key_strengths: The Governing Principle is the clearest statement of the closed-world problem in this Skill set, and the four-way triage ordered by frequency (doublets, low-quality, batch, ambient) is a prior an agent cannot derive from the data.

Two pieces of concrete tool guidance paid for themselves in execution: majority_voting took CellTypist lineage accuracy from 0.892 to 1.000 on 6,049 cells, and de.method='classic' for a bulk reference beat 'wilcox' 0.906 to 0.534 while running four times faster.
The normalization-requirements table's requirement column is correct for all four tools, and the requirements are exactly what silently breaks annotations.
The 'calibrate, do not port' rejection table is borne out: on real PBMC 1k data Azimuth's prediction score and mapping score flagged 21.9% and 0% of cells respectively and correlated at only 0.384.

recommendations.title: The triage screens on the one signal artifacts do not trip
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md:138-139 screens for suspect clusters with median conf_score < 0.5. On a dataset containing labelled doublet and low-quality clusters, that screen selected six ordinary clusters and none of the four artifact clusters, which scored 0.59 to 0.97.
recommendations.root_cause: Self-contradiction: the Skill's own Governing Principle says a state outside the reference is forced to the nearest label 'often with high apparent confidence', which is precisely why artifact clusters are confident. Low confidence instead tracks fine-granularity ambiguity between similar reference labels.
recommendations.fix: Invert the entry point. Screen every cluster on the QC covariates the same code block already computes - pct_counts_mt, n_genes_by_counts, doublet rate, batch purity - and use low annotation confidence only as a secondary signal for 'not in reference'. In this run the QC columns separated the artifacts perfectly (21-22% mito against a 2.5% baseline; doublet rates 0.44 and 0.22 against 0.02).

recommendations.title: Two 'wrong input' symptoms are stale for current tool versions
recommendations.problem: The normalization table says wrong CellTypist input produces 'confident but degraded/wrong labels, no error'; Common Errors row 3 says an Ensembl-ID query produces 'confident but nonsensical labels'. Under celltypist 1.7.1 both raise hard ValueErrors instead.
recommendations.root_cause: The symptoms were written against an older CellTypist that did not validate its input; the requirements themselves are still right.
recommendations.fix: Update both symptom cells to name the actual error strings ('Invalid expression matrix in .X, expect log1p normalized expression to 10000 counts per cell' and 'No features overlap with the model. Please provide gene symbols'), and keep a line for the case that IS still silent - log1p without CP10K, or scanpy's median-normalized default, where accuracy degrades and mean max-probability roughly halves.

recommendations.title: SingleR's rejection set is presented as a safety net it is not
recommendations.problem: The Skill treats pruned.labels and pruneScores(nmads=3) as the rejection mechanism. On a query where 169 of 3,023 cells were confidently misassigned across lineage boundaries, pruning flagged 15 cells and pruneScores flagged 0, and accuracy among retained cells was no better than overall.
recommendations.root_cause: Delta-based pruning detects cells whose best and second-best scores are close, not cells whose reference simply lacks their type - a different failure from the one the Skill is guarding against.
recommendations.fix: Say what pruning does and does not catch, and pair it with the marker-triangulation step the Skill already describes: a DotPlot of canonical markers by SingleR label would have shown the monocyte-to-B_cell assignments immediately.

recommendations.title: The marker-validation snippet assumes a normalized object it is not given
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md:155-158 runs DotPlot straight after the annotation block. On the object RunAzimuth returns, the RNA data layer is empty, and Seurat falls back with 'data layer is not found and counts layer is used' - so the validation plot is built from raw counts.
recommendations.root_cause: The validation section was written as if the object had already been through NormalizeData, which the Azimuth path does not guarantee.
recommendations.fix: Add NormalizeData(seurat_obj) (or a note that DotPlot needs the data layer) immediately above the DotPlot call.

recommendations.title: majority_voting's over-clustering is neither created nor seeded
recommendations.problem: The CellTypist snippet passes majority_voting=True but never says where the over-clustering comes from. Left to itself CellTypist runs its own Leiden; given an unseeded upstream clustering, the smoothed labels differ between runs of the same script.
recommendations.root_cause: The dependency on a clustering is implicit in the argument name.
recommendations.fix: Pass over_clustering='leiden' explicitly in the snippet and note that the upstream clustering must be seeded for the annotation to be reproducible.
